rounds.text: Krishanveer Forge Ltd trades at an attractive P/E of 16.9x [E1] and a lower multiple of 12.88x compared to the sector benchmark of 23.87x [E6]. The company exhibits exceptional capital efficiency, with an ROCE of 26.6% [E12] and an ROE of 16.9% [E13], significantly outperforming the sector benchmark ROCE of 12.66% [E10] and ROE of 10.59% [E9]. Long-term performance underscores robust fundamental compounding, evidenced by 10-year compounded sales growth of 22% [E14] and 10-year compounded profit growth of 25% [E18]. Furthermore, the discounted cash flow model suggests a substantial margin of safety of 63.5% [E44] against the current market price of ₹ 139 [E2], while the reverse DCF implies that today's price requires only a modest 3.1% earnings growth [E45]. The business is conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of -0.04x [E38] and maintains a healthy dividend payout of 44.1% [E57]. Finally, the overarching macro backdrop remains supportive, as the Capital Goods sector operates in a clear tailwind with a score of +1.04 [E69, E70]. Conceded: cash conversion is weak at 0.18x of reported profit for Mar 2026 [E34].

Sales growth has slowed significantly to just 3% over the last three years [E16], with recent performance showing a year-over-year decline in both sales and net profit [E65, E66]. The quality of reported earnings is highly suspect, as cash conversion stands at a meager 0.18x [E34], and operating cash flow represents only 35% of operating profit [E37]. Furthermore, the bottom line is bolstered by Rs. 4.17 Cr in other income [E59], which masks a cyclical earnings profile [E56] and a deceleration in core earnings growth [E67]. Investors face extreme risk through an annualized volatility of 118.7% [E52] and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -75.9% [E51]. This fundamental deterioration is reflected in the technicals, as the price has fallen below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E48, E68]. Conceded: the company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio [E38], high reported ROCE of 26.6% [E12], and trades at a P/E of 16.9x [E1], which is below the sector benchmark [E6].

Conceded: 3-year sales growth is 3% [E16] and recent sales and net profit show a year-over-year decline [E65, E66]. However, this near-term softness completely ignores the exceptional multi-year compounding power of the business, featuring 10-year sales growth at 22% [E14] and 10-year profit growth at 25% [E18]. Conceded: cash conversion is 0.18x and operating cash flow is 35% of operating profit [E34, E37]. Yet the firm remains conservatively financed with a net debt-to-equity ratio of -0.04x [E38] and has successfully improved its working capital requirements from 78.7 days down to 60.2 days [E58]. Conceded: earnings include Rs. 4.17 Cr in other income [E59] and the technicals show the price below its moving averages [E48, E68]. Nevertheless, operating margins have expanded by 6 percentage points in the TTM period to 14% [E30], backed by a stellar ROCE of 26.6% [E12] that crushes the sector benchmark of 12.66% [E10]. Finally, the drastic historical drawdown and volatility [E51, E52] are mitigated by a massive DCF margin of safety of 63.5% [E44] and a healthy dividend payout of 44.1% [E57] supported by the broader Capital Goods sector tailwind [E70].

Conceded: 10-year sales and profit growth stand at 22% and 25% respectively [E14, E18]. However, leaning on these long-term figures masks severe recent deceleration, evidenced by a 3-year compounded sales growth of just 3% [E16] alongside year-over-year declines in net profit and sales [E65, E66]. Conceded: ROCE reaches 26.6% [E12] and TTM operating margins expanded by 6 percentage points [E30]. Yet, this profitability is severely undermined by poor earnings quality, as earnings include Rs. 4.17 Cr in other income [E59], and cash conversion is alarmingly weak at 0.18x with operating cash flow representing only 35% of operating profit [E34, E37]. Conceded: the balance sheet maintains a negative net debt-to-equity ratio of -0.04x [E38].
